Main.sentence: The Communist Party of China ( CPC ), [c]  commonly known as the Chinese Communist Party ( CCP ),  is the founding and ___E:ruling party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-party_state)___ of the ___E:People's Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China)___ (PRC).

Founded in 1921, the CCP won the ___E:Chinese Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Civil_War)___ against the ___E:Kuomintang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuomintang)___ and ___E:proclaimed the establishment of the PRC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China)___ under the ___E:chairmanship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ of ___E:Mao Zedong U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong)___ in October 1949. The CCP has since governed China and has had sole control over the country's ___E:armed forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Liberation_Army)___ and ___E:law enforcement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_China)___ .

As of 2024 [update] , the CCP has more than 100 million members, making it the ___E:second largest political party by membership in the world U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_political_parties)___ .

In 1921, ___E:Chen Duxiu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Duxiu)___ and ___E:Li Dazhao U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Dazhao)___ founded the CCP with the help of the Far Eastern Bureau of the ___E:Russian Communist Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union)___ ( ___E:Bolsheviks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolsheviks)___ ) and ___E:Far Eastern Bureau of the Communist International U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far_Eastern_Bureau_of_the_Communist_International)___ .

Although the CCP aligned with the Kuomintang (KMT) during its initial years, the rise of the KMT's right-wing under the leadership of ___E:Chiang Kai-shek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiang_Kai-shek)___ and subsequent massacres of tens of thousands of CCP members resulted in a split and a prolonged civil war between the CCP and KMT. During the next ten years of ___E:guerrilla warfare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_warfare)___ , Mao Zedong rose to become the most influential figure in the CCP and the party established a strong base among the rural ___E:peasantry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peasant)___ with its ___E:land reform policies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_Reform_Movement_(China))___ .
Support for the CCP continued to grow throughout the ___E:Second Sino-Japanese War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War)___ .

After the ___E:Japanese surrender U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrender_of_Japan)___ in 1945, the CCP emerged triumphant in ___E:the communist revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Revolution)___ against the ___E:Nationalist government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalist_government)___ .

The CCP established the People's Republic of China on 1 October 1949 and the remnants of the ___E:Nationalist government retreated to Taiwan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retreat_of_the_government_of_the_Republic_of_China_to_Taiwan)___ shortly after.
Mao Zedong continued to be the most influential member of the CCP until ___E:his death in 1976 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Mao_Zedong)___ .

Under Mao, the party completed its land reform program, launched a series of ___E:five-year plans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five-year_plans_of_China)___ , and eventually ___E:split with the Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sino-Soviet_split)___ .

Although Mao attempted to purge the party of capitalist and ___E:reactionary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reactionary)___ elements during the ___E:Cultural Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution)___ , after his death, these policies were only briefly continued by the ___E:Gang of Four U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gang_of_Four)___ before a less radical faction seized control.

During the 1980s, ___E:Deng Xiaoping U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping)___ directed the CCP away from Maoist orthodoxy and towards a policy of ___E:economic liberalization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_economic_reform)___ .

Since the ___E:collapse of the Eastern Bloc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989)___ and the ___E:dissolution of the Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union)___ in 1991, the CCP has focused on maintaining its relations with the ruling parties of the remaining ___E:communist states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_communist_states)___ .

The CCP has also established relations with several non-communist parties, including dominant nationalist parties of many developing countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America, as well as ___E:social democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_democracy)___ parties in Europe.

As a ___E:Marxist–Leninist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marxist%E2%80%93Leninist)___ party, the Chinese Communist Party is organized based on ___E:democratic centralism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_centralism)___ , a principle that entails open policy discussion on the condition of unity among party members in upholding the agreed-upon decision.

The highest body of the CCP is the ___E:National Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Congress_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ , convened every fifth year. When the National Congress is not in session, the ___E:Central Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ is the highest body, but since that body usually only meets once a year, most duties and responsibilities are vested in the ___E:Politburo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politburo_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ and its ___E:Standing Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politburo_Standing_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ .
Members of the latter are seen as the top leadership of the party and the state.

Today the ___E:party's leader U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leader_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ holds the offices of ___E:general secretary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ (responsible for civilian party duties, also the ___E:top rank official U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_precedence_in_China)___ ), ___E:chairman of the Central Military Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Central_Military_Commission_(China))___ (CMC) (responsible for military affairs), and ___E:president of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_China)___ (a largely ceremonial position).
Because of these posts, the party leader is seen as the country's de facto " ___E:paramount leader U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_leader)___ ".

The current leader is ___E:Xi Jinping U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping)___ , who was elected at the 1st Plenary Session of the ___E:18th Central Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/18th_Central_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ held on 15 November 2012 and has been reelected twice, on 25 October 2017 by the ___E:19th Central Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/19th_Central_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ and on 10 October 2022 by the ___E:20th Central Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Central_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ .

The ___E:October Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_Revolution)___ and ___E:Marxist theory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marxist_philosophy)___ inspired the founding of the CCP.  : 114 ___E:Chen Duxiu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Duxiu)___ and ___E:Li Dazhao U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Dazhao)___ were among the first to publicly support ___E:Leninism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leninism)___ and ___E:world revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_revolution)___ .
Both regarded the October Revolution in Russia as groundbreaking, believing it to herald a new era for oppressed countries everywhere.

Some historical analysis views the ___E:May Fourth Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_Fourth_Movement)___ as the beginning of the revolutionary struggle that led to the ___E:founding of the People's Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China)___ .  : 22 Following the movement, trends towards social transformation increased.  : 14 Writing in 1939, Mao Zedong stated that the Movement had shown that the ___E:bourgeois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourgeoisie)___ revolution against imperialism and China had developed to a new stage, but that the ___E:proletariat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proletariat)___ would lead the revolution's completion.  : 20 The May Fourth Movement led to the establishment of radical intellectuals who went on to mobilize peasants and workers into the CCP and gain the organizational strength that would solidify the success of the ___E:Chinese Communist Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Revolution)___ .

Chen and Li were among the most influential promoters of Marxism in China during the May Fourth period.  : 7 The CCP itself embraces the May Fourth Movement and views itself as part of the movement's legacy.  : 24
Study circles were, according to ___E:Cai Hesen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cai_Hesen)___ , "the rudiments [of our party]".

Several study circles were established during the ___E:New Culture Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Culture_Movement)___ , but by 1920 many grew sceptical about their ability to bring about reforms.

China's intellectual movements were fragmented in the early 1920s.  : 17 The May Fourth Movement and the New Culture Movement had identified issues of broad concern to Chinese progressives, including ___E:anti-imperialism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-imperialism)___ , support for ___E:nationalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_nationalism)___ , support for ___E:democracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democracy_in_China)___ , promotion of feminism, and rejection of traditional values.  : 17 Proposed solutions among Chinese progressives differed significantly, however.  : 17

The CCP was founded on 1 July 1921 with the help of the Far Eastern Bureau of the ___E:Russian Communist Party (Bolsheviks) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union)___ and ___E:Far Eastern Secretariat of the Communist International U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Far_Eastern_Bureau_of_the_Communist_International)___ , according to the party's official account of its history.

However, party documents suggest that the party's actual founding date was 23 July 1921, the first day of the ___E:1st National Congress of the CCP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_National_Congress_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ .

The founding National Congress of the CCP was held 23–31 July 1921.  [better source needed] With only 50 members in the beginning of 1921, among them Chen Duxiu, Li Dazhao and Mao Zedong,  the CCP organization and authorities grew tremendously.  : 115 While it was originally held in ___E:a house U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Site_of_the_First_National_Congress_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ in the ___E:Shanghai French Concession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_French_Concession)___ , French police interrupted the meeting on 30 July  and the congress was moved to a tourist boat on ___E:South Lake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Lake_(Jiaxing))___ in ___E:Jiaxing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiaxing)___ , Zhejiang province.
A dozen delegates attended the congress, with neither Li nor Chen being able to attend,  the latter sending a personal representative in his stead.

The resolutions of the congress called for the establishment of a ___E:communist party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_party)___ as a branch of the ___E:Communist International U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_International)___ (Comintern) and elected Chen as its leader.
Chen then served as the first general secretary of the CCP  and was referred to as "China's Lenin". [citation needed]

The Soviets hoped to foster pro-Soviet forces in East Asia to fight against ___E:anti-communist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-communist)___ countries, particularly ___E:Japan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan)___ .
They attempted to contact the warlord ___E:Wu Peifu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu_Peifu)___ but failed.

The Soviets then contacted the ___E:Kuomintang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuomintang)___ (KMT), which was leading the ___E:Guangzhou government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_the_Republic_of_China_in_Guangzhou)___ parallel to the ___E:Beiyang government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beiyang_government)___ .

On 6 October 1923, the Comintern sent ___E:Mikhail Borodin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Borodin)___ to Guangzhou, and the Soviets established friendly relations with the KMT. The ___E:Central Committee of the CCP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ ,  Soviet leader ___E:Joseph Stalin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Stalin)___ ,  and the Comintern  all hoped that the CCP would eventually control the KMT and called their opponents "rightists".  [d] KMT leader ___E:Sun Yat-sen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Yat-sen)___ eased the conflict between the communists and their opponents.

CCP membership grew tremendously after the ___E:4th congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_National_Congress_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ in 1925, from 900 to 2,428.  The CCP still treats Sun Yat-sen as one of the founders of their movement and claim descent from him  as he is viewed as a proto-communist  and the economic element of ___E:Sun's ideology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Principles_of_the_People)___ was socialism.
Sun stated, "Our Principle of Livelihood is a form of communism".
The communists dominated the ___E:left wing of the KMT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_ideology_of_the_Kuomintang)___ and struggled for power with the party's right-wing factions.

When Sun Yat-sen died in March 1925, he was succeeded by a rightist, ___E:Chiang Kai-shek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiang_Kai-shek)___ , who initiated moves to marginalize the position of the communists.

Chiang, Sun's former assistant, was not actively anti-communist at that time,  even though he hated the theory of ___E:class struggle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_conflict)___ and the CCP's seizure of power.
The communists proposed removing Chiang's power.
When Chiang gradually gained the support of Western countries, the conflict between him and the communists became more and more intense.
Chiang asked the Kuomintang to join the Comintern to rule out the secret expansion of communists within the KMT, while Chen Duxiu hoped that the communists would completely withdraw from the KMT.
In April 1927, both Chiang and the CCP were preparing for conflict.

Fresh from the success of the ___E:Northern Expedition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Expedition)___ to overthrow the warlords, Chiang Kai-shek turned on the communists, who by now numbered in the tens of thousands across China.
Ignoring the orders of the Wuhan-based KMT government, he marched on Shanghai, a city controlled by communist militias.

Although the communists welcomed Chiang's arrival, he turned on them, ___E:massacring 5,000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_massacre_of_1927)___ [e] with the aid of the ___E:Green Gang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Gang)___ .
Chiang's army then marched on Wuhan but was prevented from taking the city by CCP General ___E:Ye Ting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ye_Ting)___ and his troops.
Chiang's allies also attacked communists; for example, in Beijing, Li Dazhao and 19 other leading communists were executed by ___E:Zhang Zuolin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Zuolin)___ .

Angered by these events, the peasant movement supported by the CCP became more violent. ___E:Ye Dehui U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ye_Dehui)___ , a famous scholar, was killed by communists in ___E:Changsha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changsha)___ , and in revenge, KMT general ___E:He Jian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He_Jian)___ and his troops gunned down hundreds of peasant militiamen.
That May, tens of thousands of communists and their sympathizers were killed by KMT troops, with the CCP losing approximately 15,000 of its 25,000 members.

The CCP continued supporting the Wuhan KMT government,  but on 15 July 1927 the Wuhan government expelled all communists from the KMT.  The CCP reacted by founding the ___E:Workers' and Peasants' Red Army of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Red_Army)___ , better known as the "Red Army", to battle the KMT. A battalion led by General ___E:Zhu De U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_De)___ was ordered to take the city of ___E:Nanchang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanchang)___ on 1 August 1927 in what became known as the ___E:Nanchang uprising U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanchang_uprising)___ .

Initially successful, Zhu and his troops were forced to retreat after five days, marching south to ___E:Shantou U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shantou)___ , and from there being driven into the wilderness of ___E:Fujian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fujian)___ .  ___E:Mao Zedong U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong)___ was appointed commander-in-chief of the Red Army, and led four regiments against Changsha in the ___E:Autumn Harvest Uprising U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autumn_Harvest_Uprising)___ , hoping to spark peasant uprisings across Hunan.
His plan was to attack the KMT-held city from three directions on 9 September, but the Fourth Regiment deserted to the KMT cause, attacking the Third Regiment.

Mao's army made it to Changsha but could not take it; by 15 September, he accepted defeat, with 1,000 survivors marching east to the ___E:Jinggang Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinggang_Mountains)___ of ___E:Jiangxi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangxi)___ .
The near destruction of the CCP's urban organizational apparatus led to institutional changes within the party.

The party adopted ___E:democratic centralism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_centralism)___ , a way to organize revolutionary parties, and established a politburo to function as the standing committee of the central committee.
The result was increased centralization of power within the party.
At every level of the party this was duplicated, with standing committees now in effective control.

After being expelled from the party, Chen Duxiu went on to lead China's ___E:Trotskyist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trotskyism)___ movement. ___E:Li Lisan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Lisan)___ was able to assume de facto control of the party organization by 1929–1930.

The 1929 ___E:Gutian Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gutian_Congress)___ was important in establishing the principle of party control over the military, which continues to be a core principle of the party's ideology.  : 280
Li's leadership was a failure, leaving the CCP on the brink of destruction.

The Comintern became involved, and by late 1930, his powers had been taken away.  By 1935, Mao had become a member of ___E:Politburo Standing Committee of the CCP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politburo_Standing_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ and the party's informal military leader, with ___E:Zhou Enlai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_Enlai)___ and ___E:Zhang Wentian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Wentian)___ , the formal head of the party, serving as his informal deputies.
The conflict with the KMT led to the reorganization of the Red Army, with power now centralized in the leadership through the creation of CCP political departments charged with supervising the army.

The ___E:Xi'an Incident U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi%27an_Incident)___ of December 1936 paused the conflict between the CCP and the KMT.  Under pressure from Marshal ___E:Zhang Xueliang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Xueliang)___ and the CCP, Chiang Kai-shek finally agreed to a ___E:Second United Front U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_United_Front)___ focused on repelling the Japanese invaders.

While the front formally existed until 1945, all collaboration between the two parties had effectively ended by 1940.  Despite their formal alliance, the CCP used the opportunity to expand and carve out independent bases of operations to prepare for the coming war with the KMT.  In 1939, the KMT began to restrict CCP expansion within China.
This led to frequent clashes between CCP and KMT forces  which subsided rapidly on the realization on both sides that civil war amidst a foreign invasion was not an option.
By 1943, the CCP was again actively expanding its territory at the expense of the KMT.

Mao Zedong became the Chairman of the ___E:Politburo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politburo_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ in 1943 and the ___E:Chairman of the Central Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ in 1945. After the ___E:Japanese surrender U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_surrender)___ in 1945, the war between the CCP and the KMT began again in earnest.
The 1945–1949 period had four stages; the first was from August 1945 (when the Japanese surrendered) to June 1946 (when the peace talks between the CCP and the KMT ended).
By 1945, the KMT had three times more soldiers under its command than the CCP and initially appeared to be prevailing.
With the cooperation of the US and Japan, the KMT was able to retake major parts of the country.
However, KMT rule over the reconquered territories proved unpopular because of its endemic ___E:political corruption U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_corruption)___ .
Notwithstanding its numerical superiority, the KMT failed to reconquer the rural territories which made up the CCP's stronghold.
Around the same time, the CCP launched an invasion of ___E:Manchuria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchuria)___ , where they were assisted by the Soviet Union.

The second stage, lasting from July 1946 to June 1947, saw the KMT extend its control over major cities such as ___E:Yan'an U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yan%27an)___ , the CCP headquarters, for much of the war.  The KMT's successes were hollow; the CCP had tactically withdrawn from the cities, and instead undermined KMT rule there by instigating protests among students and intellectuals.
The KMT responded to these demonstrations with heavy-handed repression.
In the meantime, the KMT was struggling with factional infighting and Chiang Kai-shek's autocratic control over the party, which weakened its ability to respond to attacks.

The third stage, lasting from July 1947 to August 1948, saw a limited counteroffensive by the CCP.  The objective was clearing "Central China, strengthening North China, and recovering Northeast China."  This operation, coupled with military desertions from the KMT, resulted in the KMT losing 2 million of its 3 million troops by the spring of 1948, and saw a significant decline in support for KMT rule.  The CCP was consequently able to cut off KMT garrisons in Manchuria and retake several territories.
The last stage, lasting from September 1948 to December 1949, saw the communists go on the offensive and the collapse of KMT rule in mainland China as a whole.

Mao's ___E:proclamation of the founding of the People's Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China)___ on 1 October 1949 marked the end of the second phase of the Chinese Civil War (or the ___E:Chinese Communist Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Revolution)___ , as it is called by the CCP).

Mao proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China (PRC) before a massive crowd at Tiananmen Square on 1 October 1949. The CCP headed the ___E:Central People's Government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_People%27s_Government_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China_(1949%E2%80%931954))___ .  : 118 From this time through the 1980s, top leaders of the CCP (such as Mao Zedong, Lin Biao, Zhou Enlai and Deng Xiaoping) were largely the same military leaders prior to the PRC's founding.
As a result, informal personal ties between political and military leaders dominated civil-military relations.

Stalin proposed a one-party constitution when ___E:Liu Shaoqi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Shaoqi)___ visited the Soviet Union in 1952.  The constitution of the PRC in 1954 subsequently abolished the previous coalition government and established the CCP's one-party system.

In 1957, the CCP launched the ___E:Anti-Rightist Campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Rightist_Campaign)___ against political dissidents and prominent figures from minor parties, which resulted in the political persecution of at least 550,000 people.

The campaign significantly damaged the limited pluralistic nature in the socialist republic and solidified the country's status as a de facto ___E:one-party state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-party_state)___ .

The Anti-Rightist Campaign led to the catastrophic results of the ___E:Second Five Year Plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_five-year_plan_(China))___ from 1958 to 1962, known as the ___E:Great Leap Forward U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Leap_Forward)___ .
In an effort to transform the country from an agrarian economy into an industrialized one, the CCP collectivized farmland, formed people's communes, and diverted labour to factories.

General mismanagement and exaggerations of harvests by CCP officials led to the ___E:Great Chinese Famine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Chinese_Famine)___ , which resulted in an estimated 15 to 45 million deaths,   making it the largest famine in recorded history.

During the 1960s and 1970s, the CCP experienced a significant ideological separation from the Communist Party of the Soviet Union which was going through a period of " ___E:de-Stalinization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De-Stalinization)___ " under ___E:Nikita Khrushchev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev)___ .

By that time, Mao had begun saying that the "continued revolution under the ___E:dictatorship of the proletariat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dictatorship_of_the_proletariat)___ " stipulated that class enemies continued to exist even though the socialist revolution seemed to be complete, leading to the ___E:Cultural Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution)___ in which millions were persecuted and killed.

During the Cultural Revolution, party leaders such as Liu Shaoqi, ___E:Deng Xiaoping U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping)___ , ___E:Peng Dehuai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peng_Dehuai)___ , and ___E:He Long U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He_Long)___ were purged or exiled, and the ___E:Gang of Four U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gang_of_Four)___ , led by Mao's wife ___E:Jiang Qing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiang_Qing)___ , emerged to fill in the power vacuum left behind.
Following Mao's death in 1976, a power struggle between CCP chairman ___E:Hua Guofeng U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hua_Guofeng)___ and vice-chairman Deng Xiaoping erupted.

Deng won the struggle, and became China's paramount leader in 1978. Shuanggui was an intra-party disciplinary process conducted by the ___E:Central Commission for Discipline Inspection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Commission_for_Discipline_Inspection)___ (CCDI).

Other reported techniques include the use of induced hallucinations, with one subject of this method reporting that "In the end I was so exhausted, I agreed to all the accusations against me even though they were false."
In 2018, the shuanggui process was superseded by liuzhi or "retention in custody", which expands beyond CCP members to the entire public sector, academics, and business leaders.

The ___E:General Office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Office_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ is the party's "nerve centre", in charge of day-to-day administrative work, including communications, protocol, and setting agendas for meetings.

The CCP currently has six main central departments: the ___E:Organization Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_Department_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ , responsible for overseeing provincial appointments and vetting cadres for future appointments,  the ___E:Publicity Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publicity_Department_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ (formerly "Propaganda Department"), which oversees the media and formulates the party line to the media,   the United Front Work Department, which oversees the country's eight minor parties, ___E:people's organizations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_organization)___ , and influence groups inside and outside of the country,  the ___E:International Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Department_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ , functioning as the party's "foreign affairs ministry" with other parties, the ___E:Society Work Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_Work_Department)___ , which handles work related to civic groups, chambers of commerce and industry groups and mixed-ownership and non-public enterprises,  and the ___E:Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Political_and_Legal_Affairs_Commission)___ , which oversees the country's legal enforcement authorities.

The CC also has direct control over the ___E:Central Policy Research Office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Policy_Research_Office)___ , which is responsible for researching issues of significant interest to the party leadership,  the ___E:Central Party School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Party_School_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party)___ , which provides political training and ideological indoctrination in communist thought for high-ranking and rising cadres,  the ___E:Institute of Party History and Literature U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Party_History_and_Literature)___ , which sets priorities for scholarly research in state-run universities and the Central Party School and studies and translates the classical works of Marxism.

The party's newspaper, the People's Daily , is under the direct control of the Central Committee  and is published with the objectives "to tell good stories about China and the (Party)" and to promote its party leader.
The theoretical magazines Qiushi and Study Times are published by the Central Party School.

The ___E:China Media Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Media_Group)___ , which oversees ___E:China Central Television U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Central_Television)___ (CCTV), ___E:China National Radio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_National_Radio)___ (CNR) and ___E:China Radio International U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Radio_International)___ (CRI), is under the direct control of the Publicity Department.

The various offices of the "Central Leading Groups", such as the ___E:Hong Kong and Macau Work Office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong_and_Macau_Work_Office)___ , the ___E:Taiwan Affairs Office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan_Affairs_Office)___ , and the Central Finance Office, also report to the central committee during a plenary session.

Additionally, per the principle of " ___E:the Party commands the gun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Party_commands_the_gun)___ ", CCP has sole control over the People's Liberation Army (PLA) through its Central Military Commission.
After seizing political power, the CCP extended the dual party-state command system to all government institutions, social organizations, and economic entities.

The State Council and the Supreme Court each has a ___E:party group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_group)___ , established since November 1949. Party committees permeate in every state administrative organ as well as the People's Consultation Conferences and mass organizations at all levels.

According to scholar ___E:Rush Doshi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rush_Doshi)___ , "[t]he Party sits above the state, runs parallel to the state, and is enmeshed in every level of the state."  Modelled after the Soviet ___E:Nomenklatura U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomenklatura)___ system, the party committee's organization department at each level has the power to recruit, train, monitor, appoint, and relocate these officials.

Party committees exist at the level of ___E:provinces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_China)___ , cities, ___E:counties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counties_of_China)___ , and neighbourhoods.
These committees play a key role in directing local policy by selecting local leaders and assigning critical tasks.
The Party secretary at each level is more senior than that of the leader of the government, with the CCP standing committee being the main source of power.

Party committee members in each level are selected by the leadership in the level above, with provincial leaders selected by the central Organizational Department, and not removable by the local party secretary.
Neighborhood committees are generally composed of older volunteers.  : 118
CCP committees exist inside of companies, both private and state-owned.
A business that has more than three party members is legally required to establish a committee or branch.
As of 2021 [update] , more than half of China's private firms have such organizations.
These branches provide places for new member socialization and host morale boosting events for existing members.
They also provide mechanisms that help private firm interface with government bodies and learn about policies which relate to their fields.
On average, the profitability of private firms with a CCP branch is 12.6 per cent higher than the profitability of private firms.

Within ___E:state-owned enterprises U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State-owned_enterprises_of_China)___ , these branches are governing bodies that make important decisions and inculcate CCP ideology in employees.
Party committees or branches within companies also provide various benefits to employees.

These may include bonuses, interest-free loans, mentorship programs, and free medical and other services for those in need.  Enterprises that have party branches generally provide more expansive benefits for employees in the areas of retirement, medical care, unemployment, injury, and birth and fertility.
Increasingly, the CCP is requiring private companies to revise their charters to include the role of the party.
The funding of all CCP organizations mainly comes from state fiscal revenue.
Data for the proportion of total CCP organizations' expenditures in total China fiscal revenue is unavailable. [citation needed]

"It is my will to join the Communist Party of China, uphold the Party's program, observe the provisions of the Party constitution, fulfill a Party member's duties, carry out the Party's decisions, strictly observe Party discipline, guard Party secrets, be loyal to the Party, work hard, fight for communism throughout my life, be ready at all times to sacrifice my all for the Party and the people, and never betray the Party."

The CCP reached 100.27 million members at the end of 2024, a net increase of 1.09 million over the previous year.   It is the second largest political party in the world after India's ___E:Bharatiya Janata Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party)___ .
To join the CCP, an applicant must go through an approval process.
Adults can file applications for membership with their local party branch.
A prescreening process, akin to a background check, follows.

Next, established party members at the local branch vet applicants' behaviour and political attitudes and may make a formal inquiry to a party branch near the applicants' parents residence to vet family loyalty to communism and the party.
In 2014, only 2 million applications were accepted out of some 22 million applicants.
Admitted members then spend a year as a probationary member.
Probationary members are typically accepted into the party.
In contrast to the past, when emphasis was placed on the applicants' ideological criteria, the current CCP stresses technical and educational qualifications.
To become a probationary member, the applicant must take an admission oath before the party flag.  The relevant CCP organization is responsible for observing and educating probationary members.
Probationary members have duties similar to those of full members, with the exception that they may not vote in party elections nor stand for election.
Many join the CCP through the ___E:Communist Youth League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Youth_League_of_China)___ .
Under Jiang Zemin, private entrepreneurs were allowed to become party members.
As of December 2024 [update] , individuals who identify as farmers, herdsmen and fishermen make up 26.1 million members; members identifying as workers totalled 6.6 million.

Another group, the "Managing, professional and technical staff in enterprises and public institutions", made up 16.4 million, 11.6 million identified as working in administrative staff and 7.6 million described themselves as party cadres.
The CCP systematically recruits ___E:white-collar workers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-collar_worker)___ over other social groups.
By 2024, CCP membership had become more educated, younger, and less blue-collar than previously, with 57.6% of party members having a college degree or above.
As of 2022 [update] , around 30 to 35 per cent of Chinese entrepreneurs are or have been a party member.
At the end of 2024, the CCP stated that it has approximately 7.73 million ethnic minority members or 7.7% of the party.
As of 2024 [update] , 30.99 million women are CCP members, representing 30.9% of the party.
Women in China have low participation rates as political leaders.
Women's disadvantage is most evident in their severe underrepresentation in the more powerful political positions.
At the top level of decision making, no woman has ever been among the members of the Politburo Standing Committee, while the broader Politburo currently does not have any female members.

Just 3 of 27 government ministers are women, and importantly, since 1997, China has fallen to 53rd place from 16th in the world in terms of female representation in the National People's Congress, according to the Inter-Parliamentary Union.
CCP leaders such as Zhao Ziyang have vigorously opposed the participation of women in the political process.
Within the party women face a ___E:glass ceiling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glass_ceiling)___ .
A 2019 ___E:Binghamton University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binghamton_University)___ study found that CCP members gain a 20% wage premium in the market over non-members.
A subsequent academic study found that the economic benefit of CCP membership is strongest on those in lower wealth brackets.
CCP households also tend to accumulate wealth faster than non-CCP households.
Certain CCP cadres have access to a ___E:special supply system U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_supply_system_of_China)___ for foodstuffs called tegong .
CCP leadership cadres have access to a dedicated ___E:healthcare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare_in_China)___ system managed by the CCP General Office.
CCP membership additionally comes with several responsibilities.
CCP members are required to give between 0.5% and 2% of their monthly salary as membership fee, which goes to the party funds.
Members must pay dues regardless of location.
They additionally need to regularly attend party meetings and basic organizational cell activities.
In 2019, the CCP Central Committee issued a rule requiring members abroad to contact CCP cells at home at least once every six months.
Failure to pay dues for six consecutive months is grounds for expulsion, according to party regulations.
The Communist Youth League (CYL) is the CCP's ___E:youth wing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth_wing)___ , and the largest mass organization for youth in China.

To join, an applicant has to be between the ages of 14 and 28.  It controls and supervises ___E:Young Pioneers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Pioneers_of_China)___ , a youth organization for children below the age of 14.  The organizational structure of CYL is an exact copy of the CCP's; the highest body is the National Congress, followed by the Central Committee, Politburo, and the Politburo Standing Committee.
However, the Central Committee (and all central organs) of the CYL work under the guidance of the CCP central leadership.
By the end of 2024, the CYLC had 75 million members and 4.4 million organizations throughout China.

At the beginning of its history, the CCP did not have a single official standard for the flag, but instead allowed individual party committees to copy the flag of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.

The Central Politburo decreed the establishment of a sole official flag on 28 April 1942: "The flag of the CPC has the length-to-width proportion of 3:2 with a ___E:hammer and sickle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hammer_and_sickle)___ in the upper-left corner, and with no five-pointed star. The Political Bureau authorizes the General Office to custom-make a number of standard flags and distribute them to all major organs".

According to the People's Daily , "The red color symbolizes revolution; the hammer-and-sickle are tools of workers and peasants, meaning that the Communist Party of China represents the interests of the masses and the people; the yellow color signifies brightness."

There is a considerable degree of interest in Cuba within the CCP.  ___E:Fidel Castro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro)___ , the former ___E:First Secretary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Secretary_of_the_Communist_Party_of_Cuba)___ of the ___E:Communist Party of Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Cuba)___ (PCC), is greatly admired, and books have been written focusing on the successes of the ___E:Cuban Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Revolution)___ .  ___E:Communication between the CCP and the PCC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93Cuba_relations)___ has increased since the 1990s.

Since the decline and fall of communism in Eastern Europe, the CCP has begun establishing party-to-party relations with non-communist parties.

These relations are sought so that the CCP can learn from them.  For instance, the CCP has been eager to understand how the ___E:People's Action Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Action_Party)___ of Singapore (PAP) maintains its total domination over ___E:Singaporean politics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_Singapore)___ through its "low-key presence, but total control."  According to the CCP's own analysis of Singapore, the PAP's dominance can be explained by its "well-developed social network, which controls constituencies effectively by extending its tentacles deeply into society through branches of government and party-controlled groups."  While the CCP accepts that Singapore is a ___E:liberal democracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_democracy)___ , they view it as a ___E:guided democracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guided_democracy)___ led by the PAP.  Other differences are, according to the CCP, "that it is not a political party based on the working class—instead it is a political party of the elite. ...

It is also a political party of the ___E:parliamentary system U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_system)___ , not a ___E:revolutionary party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanguard_party)___ ."  Other parties which the CCP studies and maintains strong party-to-party relations with are the ___E:United Malays National Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Malays_National_Organization)___ , which has ruled ___E:Malaysia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia)___ (1957–2018, 2020–2022), and the ___E:Liberal Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Democratic_Party_(Japan))___ in Japan, which dominated ___E:Japanese politics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_politics)___ since 1955.
Since Jiang Zemin's time, the CCP has made friendly overtures to its erstwhile foe, the Kuomintang.
The CCP emphasizes strong party-to-party relations with the KMT so as to strengthen the probability of the reunification of Taiwan with mainland China.
However, several studies have been written on the KMT's loss of power in 2000 after having ruled Taiwan since 1949 (the KMT officially ruled mainland China from 1928 to 1949).

In general, one-party states or dominant-party states are of special interest to the party and party-to-party relations are formed so that the CCP can study them. Circa 2008, the CCP has been especially interested in Latin America,  as shown by the increasing number of delegates sent to and received from these countries.
Of special fascination for the CCP is the 71-year-long rule of the ___E:Institutional Revolutionary Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutional_Revolutionary_Party)___ (PRI) in Mexico.

While the CCP attributed the PRI's long reign in power to the strong presidential system, tapping into the ___E:machismo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machismo)___ culture of the country, its nationalist posture, its close identification with the rural populace and the implementation of ___E:nationalization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalization)___ alongside the ___E:marketization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketization)___ of the ___E:economy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Mexico)___ ,  the CCP concluded that the PRI failed because of the lack of inner-party democracy, its pursuit of ___E:social democracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_democracy)___ , its rigid party structures that could not be reformed, its ___E:political corruption U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corruption_in_Mexico)___ , the pressure of globalization, and American interference in ___E:Mexican politics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_politics)___ .

While the CCP was slow to recognize the ___E:pink tide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pink_tide)___ in Latin America, it has strengthened party-to-party relations with several socialist and ___E:anti-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-American)___ political parties over the years.

The CCP has occasionally expressed some irritation over ___E:Hugo Chávez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Ch%C3%A1vez)___ 's ___E:anti-capitalist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-capitalist)___ and anti-American rhetoric.

Despite this, the CCP reached an agreement in 2013 with the ___E:United Socialist Party of Venezuela U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Socialist_Party_of_Venezuela)___ (PSUV), which was founded by Chávez, for the CCP to educate PSUV cadres in political and social fields.
By 2008, the CCP claimed to have established relations with 99 political parties in 29 Latin American countries.
Social democratic movements in Europe have been of great interest to the CCP since the early 1980s.

With the exception of a short period in which the CCP forged party-to-party relations with far-right parties during the 1970s in an effort to halt " ___E:Soviet expansionism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_empire)___ ", the CCP's relations with European social democratic parties were its first serious efforts to establish cordial party-to-party relations with non-communist parties.
The CCP credits the European social democrats with creating a "capitalism with a human face".

Before the 1980s, the CCP had a highly negative and dismissive view of social democracy, a view dating back to the ___E:Second International U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_International)___ and the Marxist–Leninist view on the social democratic movement.
By the 1980s, that view had changed and the CCP concluded that it could actually learn something from the social democratic movement.
CCP delegates were sent all over Europe to observe.
By the 1980s, most European social democratic parties were facing electoral decline and in a period of self-reform.

The CCP followed this with great interest, laying most weight on reform efforts within the ___E:British Labour Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_Party_(UK))___ and the ___E:Social Democratic Party of Germany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Democratic_Party_of_Germany)___ .

The CCP concluded that both parties were re-elected because they modernized, replacing traditional ___E:state socialist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_socialist)___ tenets with new ones supporting ___E:privatization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privatization)___ , shedding the belief in ___E:big government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_government)___ , conceiving a new view of the ___E:welfare state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_state)___ , changing their negative views of the market and moving from their traditional support base of trade unions to entrepreneurs, the young and students.
